title: DramaRama
description: DramaRama is a full-stack AI product I'm building: a "thinking gym" that helps you work through a hard problem with a cast of twelve AI advisors, each modeled on one of the 5 Elements of Effective Thinking. You bring a problem in plain words; The Catalyst interviews you, distills it into a one-sentence problem statement, and hands you to the advisor whose method fits how you're stuck. From there you think on a node-based canvas while the advisor coaches you through a concrete thinking move and reacts to what you write. I built the Next.js dashboard, a FastAPI backend with a hexagonal architecture, Clerk authentication, a Supabase/Postgres data layer with versioned migrations, and Claude-powered streaming prompts with per-user token budgets.
perks: Full-stack AI product: Next.js, FastAPI, Supabase & Clerk
LLM prompt design, streaming responses & per-user token budgets
Per-user authorization, versioned migrations & Vercel/Railway deploys

title: Fantum
description: Fantum is a React Native (Expo) mobile app I built for a client in 2023–2024. Firebase handles sign-in, Redux Toolkit holds registration state with joi validation before submission, phone verification runs through Twilio Verify, and styling uses NativeWind (Tailwind for React Native). A Spring Boot backend was scaffolded but the app as built is Firebase-backed.

title: United Homes
description: I built the website for United Homes, a construction company in Sacramento, CA, with React and Bootstrap: a responsive layout, image carousels of completed work, and a contact form validated with joi and react-hook-form that delivers through EmailJS.

title: RCheban Towing
description: I built the website for RCheban Towing, a towing service in South Carolina, with React, Bootstrap and SCSS: a responsive layout, a contact form validated with joi that delivers through EmailJS, and smooth-scroll navigation.

title: SkyCity Trucking
description: I built and still maintain the website for SkyCity Trucking, a transportation company in Washington, DC, using React, Bootstrap and Tailwind. It's translated with i18next so visitors can read it in their preferred language, and it has contact and job-application forms with validation and reCAPTCHA that deliver through EmailJS.
perks: Contact & application forms with reCAPTCHA and EmailJS

title: V&Y Horizon
description: I designed and built the marketing site for V&Y Horizon, a drayage and transportation company. It's a Next.js (App Router) site whose content lives in Hygraph, a headless CMS, and is fetched over GraphQL with Apollo, so the client can update headline copy, partner logos and customer reviews without touching code. The site includes a quote-request modal, a careers page with a validated application form protected by reCAPTCHA and delivered through EmailJS, a testimonial carousel, and scroll animations, all responsive across devices.
perks: Next.js App Router, React Bootstrap & Sass
Headless CMS (Hygraph) content via GraphQL & Apollo
Quote & careers forms with validation, EmailJS and reCAPTCHA

title: Accellence Craft
description: Accellence Craft is a website I built for a custom craftsmanship and remodeling contractor. It's built with Next.js and Tailwind CSS, and every piece of content (hero headers, service cards, the project gallery, the step-by-step process page and the quote banner) is modeled in Hygraph and loaded server-side through Apollo Client, so the owner can manage the whole site from a CMS. I focused on a photo-forward design with full-bleed headers, a portfolio grid of finished work, an image slider, and a navbar with a dedicated mobile menu.
perks: Apollo Client + Hygraph CMS content modeling

title: Evolution Gaming
description: I built the website for Evolution Gaming, a custom PC-building shop. It's a Next.js and Tailwind site that presents the shop's offer as a product catalog: four tiered assembly packages and a line of prebuilt PCs, each with a dynamically routed detail page generated from a single specs data file, plus financing information with Afterpay, event listings, the gaming lounge, an FAQ accordion and photo carousels of past builds. The goal was to let customers compare tiers quickly and reach out to order, so the data model, routing and layout were all designed around that comparison flow.
perks: Next.js dynamic routes driven by a specs data model
Product-catalog UX for build tiers and prebuilt PCs

title: Optimal Exterior
description: In 2022 I rebuilt the website for Optimal Exterior, an exterior-cleaning company in Houston, TX, in React and Bootstrap, working from a UX designer's layouts: a responsive design, a customer-reviews section, and a quote-request form that emails the company. The company has since moved to a different site; the link here is my build.
perks: Built from a UX designer's layouts

title: Tetris
description: Fresh out of Unity Game Development and Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF), I moved onto Vanilla Javascript and built a Tetris Clone. Throughout the process, I learned how to use visual studio code and CSS animations in making the game look more beautiful.

title: Asteroids
description: Having just moved from Unity to Windows Presentation Foundation, I learned how to work with a Graphic User Interface (GUI) such as XAML and also how to connect it to my actual code. The language that I used was C#. Because Javascript is very similar to C#, I was able to pick it up very easy as I moved on to Web Development.
perks: Dealt with Big-O and memory leaks

title: Dijkstra Visualizer
description: Dijkstra's algorithm allows us to find the shortest path between any two vertices of a graph. With this project, I created a program that displays and visualizes the algorithm. The purpose of the program is to show how Dijkstra's algorithm works through a visual context. Like all paths, this program allows the user to add barriers to the target position, and then after running the algorithm, visualizes the fastest route.
